in_pool_duplication_adjudication.adjudication: SAME_MECHANISM_CLUSTER_AT_MOST_ONE_SELECTABLE. All three trade one economic hypothesis - post-idio-shock liquidity-provision reversion, i.e. the packet's single priority search space 'idiosyncratic sector-shock reversal with market return removed before ranking'. They differ in signal standardization (A4: raw -2.0% single-day residual; A5: sigma-standardized z <= -3.0 single-day residual; A6: -5.0% cumulative 5-session TR differential without beta estimation), holding horizon (3/5/20 sessions), and book architecture (EW-10 overlay at scaled gross vs standalone 0.5-gross event book vs 2x0.40 event book). They are therefore NOT literal pseudo-replicates (different event definitions and horizon economics, so their scores are not interchangeable), but selecting two would spend 2 of the 2-family budget on one hypothesis and double-count one mechanism against the six-cell budget - functionally pseudo-replication at the hypothesis level. A1 should select at most one member of this cluster.

ranking_within_cluster.why: sigma-standardized trigger makes the event definition scale-free and cross-regime comparable (A4's fixed -2% and A6's fixed -5% thresholds are regime-fragile); the sign-inverted control is the sharpest mechanism test of the three (transitory-overshoot reversion implies sign symmetry; drift stories pay both sides); the constant-scale risk-matched benchmark cleanly separates beta; turnover is structurally guaranteed by the 5/252 budget rather than hoped for from threshold depth (A6's weakness); honest fold-1 concentration statement. Cost: open-fill execution needs plumbing resolution (A4 uses canonical close fills) - a bounded implementation fix, not a design defect.

best implementation safety of the three (canonical close fills, identical-scaling beta cancellation is the airtightest construction in the pool, shared-base control differencing) and structurally capped turnover; but the fixed raw-percentage trigger is the weakest event definition in the cluster and its demanded per-event effect size (~70 bps in 3 sessions at stress) is the most demanding in the pool. A1 preferring rubric item 6 (implementation risk) over trigger robustness could reasonably reverse ranks 1-2; on mechanism-test quality A5 leads.

most careful trigger isolation in principle (non-systemic SPY filter prevents crash-beta contamination; cumulative 5-day window matches multi-day rotation flow) but weakest on event sufficiency (possible empty fold, predeclared death), the only cluster member with no structural turnover governor, and a benchmark gross-path mischaracterization; identification leans entirely on the mirror control.

other_in_pool_relations: SFV3-A4-QEND-FLOW-REBAL vs SFV3-A6-TOM-SETTLE: both calendar-seasonality families but genuinely distinct mechanisms (quarter-boundary cross-sectional loser unwind vs month-turn uniform settlement concentration; different windows, channels, book constructions). Not pseudo-replicates; selecting both would not double-count one hypothesis, though it would concentrate the whole budget in calendar seasonality.

SFV3-A5-MKT-SHOCK-DIFFUSION vs the idio cluster: genuinely distinct mechanism class (cross-autocovariance lead-lag catch-up vs own-shock reversion), explicitly separated in Lo-MacKinlay (1990) which the proposal cites for exactly this purpose. No conflict.
